name: rod-listener-doh
description: The official doh listener: the DNS grammar over RFC 8484 and the UDP variant, answered by the kernel over the listener bridge.

opsec.notes: Operator-side infrastructure, not target-side: the package lands as a framework-dependent .NET assembly tree under the teamserver's module store (the kernel host always carries the runtime) and runs as a supervised child, binding one DoH front and one UDP socket per listener. The DoH face is always TLS -- server leaf only, no client certificate anywhere, issued by the engagement CA and handed over as a user-only PEM, so the resolver front does not fingerprint the DNS carriage; the UDP face is the classic datagram shape. The process itself parses no rod.v1 grammar, holds no engagement key, and learns no implant identity; the grammar stays id-only exactly as the in-tree DNS family kept it, and out-of-zone queries are REFUSED like any resolver refusing to be an open one.
